messages:
Riley Torres: Hi team — new hire payroll/benefits questions after week 1. I'm an international hire (EU contract) so a couple of specifics: 1) Will my medical plan be the same US plan or do I get a local/international option? 2) I paid €85 for a train to the office for onboarding — what's the process for reimbursing foreign currency? 3) My offer mentioned pro-rated company holidays — how does that apply if I started mid-year in a different country? Thanks!

Lina Patel (People Ops): welcome Riley! good Qs. Short answers: 1) International hires have region-specific benefits. For EU-contracted employees we enroll you in our European benefits bundle (local medical + dental depending on country) rather than the US BeneCorp plan. You should get an invite to the EU benefits portal (check spam). 2) For foreign currency receipts: submit on Spendesk, attach the original receipt and the bank/card statement showing the charge. Spendesk will handle FX conversion using the transaction date. If you prefer, you can convert using the daily rate and put the EUR amount in the expense notes — finance will reconcile. 3) Holidays: we follow the local country holiday calendar for international hires. Company-wide fixed days (e.g., company winter closure) are pro-rated based on your start date. PTO accrual may also follow local statutory rules.

Riley Torres: Thanks. I haven't seen the EU benefits invite yet. Is there a separate deadline for enrollment for international hires?

Lina Patel: same 30-day enrollment window applies. If you don't get the invite within 48 hours, ping benefits@redwood and we'll trigger a resend. Also DM me your country so I can confirm which local bundle applies.

Riley Torres: Spain — will need partner onboarding docs for spousal coverage. Also, for the €85 train: do I need manager pre-approval? It wasn't in the original onboarding plan, I bought ticket day-of.

Priya Nair (Manager): approved for reimbursement — no pre-approval needed for small transit costs. Tag me in Spendesk and I'll approve.

Jonas Meyer (Finance): FYI for cross-border expenses: Submit the original receipt + proof of payment. If the merchant only provides a paper ticket, scan or photo is OK. Spendesk will show the converted USD value in the expense. If the amount exceeds policy thresholds (>$250 equivalent), finance may request additional justification.

Riley Torres: Great — one last payroll nuance: payroll currency. Will I be paid in EUR or USD? The offer had USD numbers but I thought EU hires get local currency?
